title: 5.4 Infectious Diseases
description: Infectious diseases, pathogens, transmission, and prevention

questions.question: What is an infectious disease?
options: A disease caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person
A disease caused by genetic factors
A disease caused by nutritional deficiency
A disease caused by chemical poisoning
questions.answer: A disease caused by disease-causing organisms that can be transmitted from person to person

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of pathogens that cause infectious diseases?
questions.answer: Bacteria, viruses, protozoa, and fungi

questions.question: Which of the following is a method of transmission for infectious diseases?
options: Direct contact with a patient, contaminated water or food, insect bites, and sexual intercourse
questions.answer: Direct contact with a patient, contaminated water or food, insect bites, and sexual intercourse

questions.question: What is a vector in the context of infectious diseases?
options: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another
A medication used to treat infections
questions.answer: An organism that carries a disease-causing organism and transmits it from one person to another

questions.question: Tuberculosis (TB) is caused by which pathogen?
questions.answer: Bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis

questions.question: How is tuberculosis (TB) primarily transmitted?
options: Through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes
questions.answer: Through airborne droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes

questions.question: What is the name of the vaccine used to prevent tuberculosis?
questions.answer: BCG vaccine

questions.question: Malaria is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.answer: Protozoan called Plasmodium

questions.question: Which mosquito species acts as a vector for malaria?
questions.answer: Female Anopheles mosquito

questions.question: Which of the following is a method to control malaria?
options: Reducing mosquito populations, avoiding mosquito bites, and using anti-malarial drugs
questions.answer: Reducing mosquito populations, avoiding mosquito bites, and using anti-malarial drugs

questions.question: What does HIV stand for?
questions.answer: Human Immunodeficiency Virus

questions.question: Which type of cells does HIV primarily infect and destroy?
questions.answer: T-lymphocytes (helper T cells)

questions.question: How is HIV transmitted?
options: Through direct exchange of body fluids such as blood, semen, and breast milk
Through casual contact like shaking hands
questions.answer: Through direct exchange of body fluids such as blood, semen, and breast milk

questions.question: Cholera is transmitted primarily through:
questions.answer: Contaminated drinking water and food

questions.question: What disease is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi?
questions.answer: Typhoid fever

questions.question: COVID-19 is caused by which virus?
questions.answer: SARS-CoV-2

questions.question: How does COVID-19 primarily spread?
options: Through respiratory droplets released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes
questions.answer: Through respiratory droplets released when an infected person breathes, talks, coughs, or sneezes

questions.question: Which of the following is a common symptom of COVID-19?
options: Fever, cough, tiredness, and loss of taste or smell
questions.answer: Fever, cough, tiredness, and loss of taste or smell

questions.question: What is the difference between an epidemic and a pandemic?
options: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or worldwide
An epidemic is more severe than a pandemic
A pandemic is limited to one region
There is no difference between them
questions.answer: A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across multiple countries or worldwide

questions.question: Vaccination works by:
options: Making the body defend against disease-causing organisms
Killing all bacteria in the body
questions.answer: Making the body defend against disease-causing organisms

questions.question: Proper waste disposal helps prevent infectious diseases by:
options: Reducing the breeding sites for pathogens and vectors
Increasing oxygen levels in the air
questions.answer: Reducing the breeding sites for pathogens and vectors
